title: Minimax ATE Estimation with Weak Proxy Outcomes and Gold-Standard Annotations over Finite Cells
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal:below-floor: mathematics and decision pass with no findings; cold review assigns subfield with paper_score_ceiling 7.2 below field threshold 7.4, salvageable=false and no improvement directive. Standing operator decision banks downgraded and stops before F1.

Scope is limited to a public homogeneous binary channel with fixed overlap; extreme calibration and exhaustive prefix averaging constrain practical significance.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the all-resource public-channel annotation frontier, including an attaining original-record estimator and matching common-marginal converse. Math and decision panels pass without findings, but the final cold review assigns subfield at 7.2, below the fixed field floor of 7.4. No conjecture collapsed; formalization was not entered and no Lean verification or F7 promotion is claimed.
tldr: For \(N=n+m\) and \(q=m+\rho^2n\), the minimax MSE over arbitrary finite-cell masses and fixed occupied-cell overlap is, up to universal constants, \(1\) for \(q\le1\) and \(\min\{1,q^{-1}+[d/(N\log(\mathrm e q))]^2\}\) for \(q>1\). A total finite original-record estimator attains this rate, and a normalized common-marginal full-record converse matches it uniformly in \(\rho\), including \(\rho=0\), \(\rho=1\), no-gold, bounded-gold, diverging \(N/q\), and null-cell regimes.
gap: Shu--Yi correct known binary outcome error under fitted propensity models. The clean annotation result separates outcomes from unmarked assignment information. Neither supplied theorem determines the unrestricted finite-cell original-record frontier when weak observations still carry attenuated outcome marks.
fill: An evaluated all-resource minimax law, total finite estimator, and matched same-class testing construction would give a prospective annotation benchmark for the outcome-error ATE problem. The logarithm and source-ratio dependence must be derived rather than substituted from a clean theorem.
